setlist_extra.title: Phil Lesh and Ned Lagin - Seastones

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Phil Lesh and Ned Lagin - Seastones** (3 reviews): A baby's wail can be heard in Seastones, most noticeable about three to five minutes in; Seastones contrasts totally with the first set and is described as very trippy [15][17][18]
- **Friend of the Devil** (1 review): Reviewer enjoyed hearing Friend of the Devil in the solid first set [9]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Reviewer liked the direction the band took Jack Straw in during this period [9]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Reviewer wonders whether Bobby is playing staccato rhythm on China Cat [12]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Phil is strong on Let It Grow and the jam is hot [17]
- **Ramble on Rose** (1 review): Keith is right on for Ramble on Rose, and Jerry handles the vocals well [17]
- **Mexicali Blues** (1 review): Attendee near the stage, in front of Bobby, heard him sound the chord while tuning and shouted the song's name [13]
- **Casey Jones** (1 review): Reviewer thinks Casey Jones sounds better here than on the Steal Your Face release [9]

## The recordings

- **gd1974-10-17.140588.SBD.Gastwirt.Miller.Noel.t-flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 28 songs; 186 min; rated 2.5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd74-10-17.sbd.barbella.16189.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 27 songs; 175 min; rated 4.33/5 by 6 [2]. Said about its sound: The Other One>Spanish Jam>Heaven Help the Fool jam>Other One sounds spectacular on the Grateful Dead Movie DVD bonus disc [10]
- **gd1974-10-17.176621.sony.ecm250.falanga.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 26 songs; 192 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd1974-10-17.sbd.smith.gems.99032.flac24**: soundboard; 25 songs; 163 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [5]. Said about its sound: Multitrack mix was remastered for tonal balance: Phil's bass reduced, buried highs restored though still somewhat distant [5]
- **gd1974-10-17.sbd.smith.gems.99031.flac16**: soundboard; 25 songs; 163 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [6]. Said about its sound: First song has right-channel trouble, like a blown stage speaker, fixed afterward; otherwise clean, clear soundboard of a relaxed show; The fallen mic causes perpetual chirping on all recordings of this night, including the hall mix and 16-track mix [12][16]

## Around the show

- Stage talk about: Bill Graham [1]
- Relaxed performance in front of the hometown crowd; reviewer wonders if Jerry plays his white Strat [12]
- Online accounts say the big boom during opening Promised Land was Keith's piano top crashing down [15]
- A mic rigged to Bobby's amp stack fell near Billy's kick seconds into Promised Land, staying unnoticed for two nights [16]
- Ned Lagin played electric piano and synthesizer on Seastones [3]
- Reviewer calls it the best show of the Winterland farewell run, with the run's single best set [19]
- Reviewer says the band reaches for adventurous material, a typical 1974 sound, and much of this show was used in the movie [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1974-10-17.140588.SBD.Gastwirt.Miller.Noel.t-flac1644**: taped by From Gastwirt Collection; transferred by Charlie Miller and Joe Noel; source: flac16/48kHz ; Soundboard > 1st gen reel > PCM > DAT; Charlie Miller [1]. Also: Sources include a Black Maxell UDII reel tape (99031) and a multitrack master reel (16189) [1]
- **gd74-10-17.sbd.barbella.16189.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [2]
- **gd1974-10-17.176621.sony.ecm250.falanga.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Louis Falanga; transferred by Bob Menke, Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: Louis Falanga's Master Audience Cassettes; Sony ECM 250 mic > Sony TC-110 (Maxell UD C120) [3]. Also: Falanga's master cassette recording, transferred by Bob Menke, is patched with soundboard material for Seastones' start, He's Gone and Other One transition [3]
- **gd1974-10-17.sbd.smith.gems.99032.flac24**: transferred by Matt Smith and Jamie Waddell; source: SBD > 16track> 2track for Jerry >? > [5]
- **gd1974-10-17.sbd.smith.gems.99031.flac16**: transferred by Matt Smith and Jamie Waddell; source: SBD > 16track> 2track for Jerry >? > [6]
